meanings: to kidnap and force people into service

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.
The character traces the head and shaft of a simple nail, a shape later borrowed for other meanings.

example.hanzi: 拉丁语是许多欧洲语言的祖先。
example.pinyin: Lādīngyǔ shì xǔduō Ōuzhōu yǔyán de zǔxiān.
example.english: Latin is the ancestor of many European languages.
example.fact: Latin was the everyday language of the Roman Empire, which at its height in the 2nd century AD stretched from Britain to Egypt. As the empire fragmented, Latin evolved regionally into French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian. Carl Linnaeus later chose Latin as the universal language for naming species in the 18th century, which is why scientific names like Homo sapiens remain in Latin today.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
木 (wood) pictures a wooden dyeing vat.
氿-shaped strokes above picture liquid dye poured into it, giving 染 its meaning 'to dye.'

example.hanzi: 感冒很容易传染给别人。
example.pinyin: Gǎnmào hěn róngyì chuánrǎn gěi biérén.
example.english: A cold is very easy to pass on to other people.
example.fact: Epidemiologists measure how contagious a disease is with a number called R0, the average number of people one sick person infects in a fully susceptible population. Measles has one of the highest known R0 values, between 12 and 18, meaning a single case can seed a dozen or more new infections before a vaccine campaign brings the outbreak under control. Ordinary seasonal influenza, by contrast, usually sits closer to an R0 of 1 to 2.

components.note: 立 (standing) — a small figure standing upright.
里 here representing a village or settlement, together giving 童 its meaning 'child.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.

example.hanzi: 那个国家的童子军大多是被绑架的儿童。
example.pinyin: Nàge guójiā de tóngzǐjūn dàduō shì bèi bǎngjià de értóng.
example.english: That country's child soldiers are mostly children who were kidnapped.
example.fact: The United Nations estimates that tens of thousands of children have been recruited into armed forces and groups in conflicts across more than a dozen countries in recent decades. In 2000, the UN adopted the Optional Protocol on the Involvement of Children in Armed Conflict, raising the minimum age for direct participation in hostilities to 18. Organizations like UNICEF run demobilization programs that combine trauma counseling with education and vocational training to help former child soldiers reintegrate into civilian life.

components.note: 亻 (person) leans to the side.
木 (tree) — a person resting against a tree gave 休 its meaning 'to rest.'
亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')

example.hanzi: 我打算下个月休假去欧洲旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn xià ge yuè xiūjià qù Ōuzhōu lǚxíng.
example.english: I plan to take vacation next month to travel to Europe.
example.fact: The European Union's Working Time Directive requires member states to guarantee workers at least four weeks of paid annual leave, a floor that countries like France and Germany exceed. The United States, by contrast, has no federal law mandating any paid vacation at all, leaving it entirely up to employers. Studies by the U.S. Travel Association have found that despite this, many American workers leave unused vacation days on the table each year rather than taking the time off.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撤 relates to physically removing or withdrawing something by hand.
The remaining element is close in sound to chè, echoing the same phonetic root found in 彻 (chè), which shares this same sound-bearing part.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.hanzi: 台风来临前，居民被迫撤离沿海地区。
example.pinyin: Táifēng láilín qián, jūmín bèipò chèlí yánhǎi dìqū.
example.english: Before the typhoon arrived, residents were forced to evacuate the coastal area.
example.fact: After the Chernobyl nuclear disaster on April 26, 1986, the nearby city of Pripyat was not evacuated for almost 36 hours, even as radiation levels climbed. When the order finally came, roughly 49,000 residents were bussed out in under three hours, told only that the evacuation was temporary — most were never allowed to return, and the city remains an abandoned time capsule inside the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone today.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'
糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'

example.hanzi: 别担心，迟到一点不要紧。
example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, chídào yìdiǎn bùyàojǐn.
example.english: Don't worry, it doesn't matter if you're a little late.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that simply being reassured by a trusted person can measurably dampen the brain's pain response, an effect documented in fMRI studies of the anterior cingulate cortex. This overlaps with the placebo effect, where inert treatments trigger real reductions in pain and anxiety simply because the recipient expects to feel better. The effect is strong enough that some hospitals now train staff in specific reassurance language to reduce patients' use of anesthesia during minor procedures.

components.note: 月 (moon) — 朝 originally depicted the sun rising while the moon was still visible, an image of early morning
龺 (an ancient form connected to dawn) gives the phonetic element for 朝's reading cháo
鱼 (fish) — 鲜 originally described fresh fish or meat.
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 鲜.

example.hanzi: 朝鲜与韩国之间的边境线是世界上戒备最森严的地区之一。
example.pinyin: Cháoxiǎn yǔ Hánguó zhījiān de biānjìngxiàn shì shìjiè shàng jièbèi zuì sēnyán de dìqū zhī yī.
example.english: The border between North Korea and South Korea is one of the most heavily guarded regions in the world.
example.fact: The Korean Demilitarized Zone is a 250-kilometer-long buffer strip roughly 4 kilometers wide that has separated North and South Korea since the 1953 armistice. Despite being lined with landmines, guard posts, and barbed wire, the near-total absence of human activity for seven decades has turned it into an accidental wildlife refuge, home to red-crowned cranes, Asiatic black bears, and possibly surviving populations of the Amur leopard.

components.note: 山 is a simple picture of three mountain peaks in a row.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 我们爬到山上看日出。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen pá dào shānshàng kàn rìchū.
example.english: We climbed up the mountain to watch the sunrise.
example.fact: Air pressure drops steadily with altitude, which is why water boils at a lower temperature the higher up a mountain you go — at the summit of Mount Everest, water boils at around 70°C instead of 100°C, making it hard to cook food properly. This same pressure drop is why climbers above roughly 8,000 meters, a zone nicknamed the 'death zone,' need supplemental oxygen just to survive.

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
⺼ (flesh) — 腕 names a body part.
宛 (wǎn) gives a sound close to wàn, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他打网球的时候不小心扭伤了手腕。
example.pinyin: Tā dǎ wǎngqiú de shíhou bù xiǎoxīn niǔshāng le shǒuwàn.
example.english: He accidentally sprained his wrist while playing tennis.
example.fact: The human wrist contains eight small carpal bones arranged in two rows, giving it an unusually wide range of motion compared to other joints. This complexity also makes it fragile: a fall onto an outstretched hand commonly causes a 'Colles' fracture' of the forearm bone near the wrist, one of the most frequent fractures seen in emergency rooms, especially in older adults with osteoporosis.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
彳 (a step/road) — 征 relates to a long journey or military campaign
正 (zhèng) gives a sound close to 征's reading zhēng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 科学家根据化石的特征判断这是一种新物种。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā gēnjù huàshí de tèzhēng pànduàn zhè shì yì zhǒng xīn wùzhǒng.
example.english: Scientists determined from the fossil's characteristics that it was a new species.
example.fact: Paleontologists classify newly found fossils by comparing distinguishing physical traits against known specimens, a method called cladistics that groups organisms by shared derived characteristics rather than superficial resemblance. This approach overturned decades of assumptions, for instance revealing that birds are more closely related to certain dinosaurs like Velociraptor than crocodiles are to those same dinosaurs.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — represents a house or enclosure sheltering what lies beneath.
The lower strokes are a simplified stand-in for the treasure (贝) that appeared under the roof in the traditional form 實, together giving 实 its meaning 'real, solid, true.'
习 is a simplified form of 習, itself composed of 羽 (feathers/wings) above 白 (sun) — a young bird practicing flight day after day under the sun, the source of 习's meaning 'to practice, to study.'

example.hanzi: 她暑假在一家科技公司实习。
example.pinyin: Tā shǔjià zài yì jiā kējì gōngsī shíxí.
example.english: She interned at a tech company over the summer.
example.fact: The modern internship traces back to medieval European guilds, where young apprentices spent years working under a master craftsman in exchange for training rather than pay. Germany's dual education system still formalizes this today: nearly half of German teenagers enter an Ausbildung, a structured multi-year apprenticeship combining paid on-the-job training with classroom study, before ever finishing what Americans would call a college degree.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 睡 relates to closing the eyes to sleep.
垂 (chuí) gives a sound partly close to shuì, sharing part of the rhyme.
目 (eye) — sleep involves closing one's eyes.
民 (mín) gives a sound close to mián, sharing the initial and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 良好的睡眠对身体健康非常重要。
example.pinyin: Liánghǎo de shuìmián duì shēntǐ jiànkāng fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.english: Good sleep is extremely important for physical health.
example.fact: During deep sleep, the brain's glymphatic system — discovered by researchers at the University of Rochester in 2012 — flushes out metabolic waste products, including beta-amyloid, a protein linked to Alzheimer's disease. Brain cells actually shrink slightly during sleep, widening the channels between them so cerebrospinal fluid can wash through more efficiently, essentially giving the brain a nightly cleaning cycle.

components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 很多网络作家不愿意公开自己的真名。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō wǎngluò zuòjiā bù yuànyì gōngkāi zìjǐ de zhēnmíng.
example.english: Many internet writers are unwilling to reveal their real names.
example.fact: The Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa took the pseudonym further than almost any writer in history, inventing more than seventy 'heteronyms' — fully realized alternate authors with their own biographies, writing styles, and even astrological charts — rather than simply hiding his real name behind a single pen name. Samuel Clemens took a simpler route, borrowing the riverboat call 'mark twain,' meaning two fathoms of water depth, for his now far more famous byline.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 购 relates to spending money to buy something.
勾 (gōu) gives a sound close to gòu, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.
买 is a simplified form of 買, originally picturing 网 (a net) above 贝 (a shell, ancient currency) — catching valuable goods to trade, the source of its meaning 'to buy.'

example.hanzi: 消费者在购买商品前应该比较价格。
example.pinyin: Xiāofèizhě zài gòumǎi shāngpǐn qián yīnggāi bǐjiào jiàgé.
example.english: Consumers should compare prices before purchasing goods.
example.fact: The barcode, first scanned commercially on a pack of Wrigley's chewing gum in an Ohio supermarket in 1974, was designed to speed up checkout and track inventory automatically. Today the same UPC and QR-code systems process billions of purchases every day worldwide, and the original 1974 gum pack is now preserved in the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恐 describes fear felt in the heart.
巩 (gǒng) gives a sound close to kǒng, sharing the same rhyme.
忄 (heart) shows 慌 relates to an emotional state.
荒 (huāng) gives the exact sound of 慌.

example.hanzi: 股市暴跌引发了投资者的恐慌。
example.pinyin: Gǔshì bàodiē yǐnfā le tóuzīzhě de kǒnghuāng.
example.english: The stock market crash triggered panic among investors.
example.fact: On October 24, 1929 — a day now remembered as 'Black Thursday' — nearly 13 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange as panicked investors rushed to sell, more than three times the normal volume. The resulting crash wiped out an estimated $30 billion in market value within days and helped trigger the decade-long Great Depression that followed.

components.note: 止 (foot) sits at the top; combined with a boat shape below, 前 originally depicted a foot stepping onto a boat, moving forward.
The lower portion is a worn-down form of 舟 (boat), from the original image of a foot boarding a boat and heading onward — the source of 前's meaning 'front, ahead.'
禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'

example.hanzi: 他因为有前科而找工作很困难。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yǒu qiánkē ér zhǎo gōngzuò hěn kùnnán.
example.english: He has trouble finding work because he has a criminal record.
example.fact: Studies on hiring discrimination have found that job applicants with a criminal record receive roughly 50 percent fewer callbacks than identical applicants without one, even when they are equally qualified. This evidence helped drive the 'Ban the Box' movement in the United States, which has led more than 35 states to remove the criminal-history checkbox from initial job applications so candidates get evaluated on qualifications first.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 忽 describes a mental state, a sudden shift in attention.
勿 (wù) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading hū has diverged.
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 我们不应该忽视气候变化带来的影响。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bù yīnggāi hūshì qìhòu biànhuà dàilái de yǐngxiǎng.
example.english: We should not neglect the effects brought by climate change.
example.fact: Since 1958, scientists atop Mauna Loa volcano in Hawaii have continuously measured atmospheric carbon dioxide levels, producing the now-famous 'Keeling Curve.' When measurements began, CO2 concentration stood at about 315 parts per million; it has since climbed past 420 parts per million, a level the planet had not seen in at least 800,000 years of ice-core records.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
升 is a pictograph of an ancient measuring ladle used to scoop out a fixed volume of grain, the source of its use as a unit of volume; the meaning 'to rise, ascend' developed later as an extension.

example.hanzi: 公司决定提升他为部门经理。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng tíshēng tā wéi bùmén jīnglǐ.
example.english: The company decided to promote him to department manager.
example.fact: In 1969, Canadian educator Laurence J. Peter coined the 'Peter Principle,' the satirical but widely studied observation that employees in a hierarchy tend to be promoted based on performance in their current role until they reach a position where they are no longer competent — and then stay there. A 2018 study analyzing sales-employee promotion data at over 200 U.S. firms found real statistical evidence supporting the idea: the best salespeople were often promoted into management roles where they performed worse than average.

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
应 is a simplified form of 應, which combined 心 (heart) with 雁 (a wild goose, serving as a sound cue) — an inner response to something outside, the source of 应's meaning 'to respond, to answer.'

example.hanzi: 这种门装有感应装置，人靠近就会自动打开。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng mén zhuāng yǒu gǎnyìng zhuāngzhì, rén kàojìn jiù huì zìdòng dǎkāi.
example.english: This kind of door has a sensor device that opens automatically when someone approaches.
example.fact: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831 by moving a magnet through a coil of wire and noticing it generated an electric current, even though the magnet and wire never touched. This single principle underlies nearly all modern electricity generation, from the giant turbines in power plants to the wireless charging pad that powers up a phone by induction alone.

components.note: 止 (foot) sits at the top; combined with a boat shape below, 前 originally depicted a foot stepping onto a boat, moving forward.
The lower portion is a worn-down form of 舟 (boat), from the original image of a foot boarding a boat and heading onward — the source of 前's meaning 'front, ahead.'
亻 (person) — 任 relates to a person taking on a responsibility or role.
壬 (rén) gives a hint of the sound — 任 is pronounced rèn, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.hanzi: 新任经理接手了前任留下的很多问题。
example.pinyin: Xīnrèn jīnglǐ jiēshǒu le qiánrèn liúxià de hěn duō wèntí.
example.english: The new manager inherited many problems left by his predecessor.
example.fact: In 1801, John Adams became the first U.S. president to hand power to a political rival, Thomas Jefferson, after losing a bitterly contested election — a peaceful transfer that was far from guaranteed to happen anywhere in the world at the time. Adams was so embittered by the loss that he skipped Jefferson's inauguration entirely, leaving Washington before dawn.

meanings: eager to do sth without delay

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — pressing close on someone's heels ties to 迫's meaning 'to press, to force.'
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pò, having drifted apart over time.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
及 pictures a hand reaching out to grab the person in front, the source of its meaning 'to reach, to catch up to,' and by extension 'up to, including.'
彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed

example.hanzi: 孩子们迫不及待地想要打开圣诞礼物。
example.pinyin: Háizimen pòbùjídài de xiǎng yào dǎkāi Shèngdàn lǐwù.
example.english: The children couldn't wait to open their Christmas presents.
example.fact: Neuroscientist Wolfram Schultz's experiments on dopamine in the 1990s revealed that the brain's reward chemical spikes most sharply in anticipation of a reward, not upon receiving it — a discovery that reshaped how psychologists understand craving and motivation. This is part of why the wait for a gift, a text message, or a paycheck can feel more intensely emotional than the moment it actually arrives.

meanings: fig. original voice of a poet

components.note: 欠 (breath, an open mouth exhaling) — 歌 relates to the breath used in singing.
哥 (gē) gives the sound — an exact match with 歌's reading gē.
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 夜晚的公园里传来悠扬的歌声。
example.pinyin: Yèwǎn de gōngyuán lǐ chuánlái yōuyáng de gēshēng.
example.english: A melodious singing voice drifted through the park at night.
example.fact: Humpback whales compose songs that can last over 30 minutes and are sung in complex, repeating patterns that spread across entire ocean populations, with all males in a region often singing a similar version that slowly evolves over years — much like a cultural trend passed from whale to whale. Researchers still don't fully agree on why they sing, though mating display and long-distance communication across dozens of kilometers of ocean are leading theories.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
虍 pictures a tiger's head and stripes.
几 below pictures its legs and tail, together giving a full picture of a tiger.

example.hanzi: 动物园里的老虎正在悠闲地散步。
example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de lǎohǔ zhèngzài yōuxián de sànbù.
example.english: The tiger at the zoo is leisurely taking a walk.
example.fact: Every tiger has a unique stripe pattern, much like a human fingerprint, and remarkably the stripes are visible even on a tiger's shaved skin, meaning the pattern is set in the skin itself rather than just the fur. Wild tiger populations have fallen by roughly 95 percent over the past century, from around 100,000 individuals in 1900 to fewer than 5,000 today, largely due to habitat loss and poaching.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 议会将在下周投票决定这项法案。
example.pinyin: Yìhuì jiāng zài xià zhōu tóupiào juédìng zhè xiàng fǎ'àn.
example.english: Parliament will vote next week to decide on this bill.
example.fact: Iceland's Althing, founded in 930 AD at Þingvellir, is widely considered the oldest parliamentary institution still functioning today, roughly 1,000 years old. Early sessions were held outdoors on a natural rock formation that let a speaker's voice carry across the assembled crowd — an ancient acoustic trick long before microphones existed.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

example.hanzi: 森林里突然发生了一场大火。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ tūrán fāshēng le yì chǎng dàhuǒ.
example.english: A large fire suddenly broke out in the forest.
example.fact: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfire season, nicknamed the 'Black Summer,' burned an estimated 18.6 million hectares — an area larger than the entire country of Syria — and was intense enough to generate its own thunderstorms, called pyrocumulonimbus clouds, that lofted smoke more than 15 kilometers into the stratosphere and circled the globe.

components.note: 龹 pictures two hands working together.
㔾 depicts a person curled up, giving 卷 its meaning of rolling or curling something up.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 他不小心卷入了一场政治丑闻。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn juǎnrù le yì chǎng zhèngzhì chǒuwén.
example.english: He accidentally got drawn into a political scandal.
example.fact: The word 'scandal' ultimately traces back to the ancient Greek skandalon, meaning a trap or stumbling block set to trip someone up. The Watergate scandal of the early 1970s, named simply after the Washington, D.C. hotel where a break-in occurred, became so culturally dominant that the '-gate' suffix has since been attached to hundreds of unrelated controversies, from 'Deflategate' to 'Bridgegate.'

components.note: 虫 (a small creature) — 蛋 names an egg, historically grouped together with small creatures like insects and reptiles.
延 (yán) is only distantly related in sound to dàn — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
虫 (a small creature) — 蛋 names an egg, historically grouped together with small creatures like insects and reptiles.
延 (yán) is only distantly related in sound to dàn — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了一下他的蛋蛋，说没有问题。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le yíxià tā de dàndàn, shuō méiyǒu wèntí.
example.english: The doctor examined his testicles and said there was no problem.
example.fact: Human testicles are held outside the main body cavity because sperm production works best at a temperature about 2-4°C cooler than core body temperature. The cremaster muscle can pull them closer to the body for warmth or let them hang lower to cool down, acting as a built-in thermostat that responds to ambient temperature within seconds.

components.note: Money/shell — ancient currency, linking to financial loss.
Gives the sound pǒu, related to péi but drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 偿 describes a person repaying something owed.
尝 (cháng) is an exact match for the sound of 偿.

example.hanzi: 保险公司同意赔偿他的医疗费用。
example.pinyin: Bǎoxiǎn gōngsī tóngyì péicháng tā de yīliáo fèiyòng.
example.english: The insurance company agreed to compensate his medical expenses.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved in Babylon around 1754 BC, is one of the earliest known legal codes to formalize compensation for harm, prescribing specific payments or penalties depending on the victim's social status and the severity of the injury. Modern compensation law still echoes this idea of proportional restitution, though it has moved away from Hammurabi's more infamous 'eye for an eye' punishments.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潜 describes hiding beneath the surface of water.
替 (tì) gives a sound distantly related to qián, having drifted apart over time.
水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在假期去海边潜水。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài jiàqī qù hǎibiān qiánshuǐ.
example.english: He likes to go diving at the seaside during vacations.
example.fact: Free-diver Herbert Nitsch set the current world record in 2007 by descending to 214 meters on a single breath, a depth at which the human body experiences immense pressure changes in just a couple of minutes. Scuba divers going that deep with compressed air risk 'nitrogen narcosis,' a state resembling drunkenness caused by nitrogen dissolving into the bloodstream under pressure, which is why deep technical dives use special gas mixes instead of ordinary air.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咒 relates to words spoken aloud, as in a chant or curse.
兄 (xiōng) is distantly close in sound to zhòu, the connection having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ

example.hanzi: 巫师念了一段神秘的咒语。
example.pinyin: Wūshī niàn le yí duàn shénmì de zhòuyǔ.
example.english: The sorcerer recited a mysterious incantation.
example.fact: Archaeologists have recovered thousands of ancient Egyptian magical papyri containing spoken incantations meant to heal illness, ward off scorpions, or curse enemies, many written in a hybrid of Egyptian and Greek. Anthropologists studying ritual language today note that the rhythmic, repetitive structure common to spells and chants across unrelated cultures — from West African praise poetry to Tibetan mantras — may work partly by inducing a measurable calming effect on the nervous system, independent of any supernatural claim.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the sea or river being traveled through
斿 — a banner streaming in the wind, evoking free, drifting movement
舟 (boat) — 艇 names a small boat or craft.
廷 (tíng) gives a sound very close to tǐng, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.

example.hanzi: 富豪们喜欢在地中海驾驶游艇度假。
example.pinyin: Fùháomen xǐhuan zài Dìzhōnghǎi jiàshǐ yóutǐng dùjià.
example.english: Wealthy people like to cruise on yachts in the Mediterranean for vacation.
example.fact: The English word 'yacht' comes from the Dutch jaghtschip, literally 'hunt ship,' originally referring to small, fast vessels the Dutch navy used to pursue pirates and smugglers along shallow coastlines in the 16th century. When King Charles II returned from exile in the Netherlands in 1660, he brought the concept — and the word — back to England, where yachting quickly became a leisure pursuit of the aristocracy rather than a naval tactic.

components.note: 今 (now, the present) — represents what is currently on one's mind.
心 (heart/mind) — keeping the present moment in mind gave 念 its meaning 'to think of, to read aloud, to study.'
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 他心里突然冒出一个奇怪的念头。
example.pinyin: Tā xīnlǐ tūrán mào chū yí ge qíguài de niàntou.
example.english: A strange thought suddenly popped into his mind.
example.fact: A 2020 study by cognitive neuroscientists at Queen's University in Canada used fMRI brain-scanning patterns to estimate that the average person experiences roughly 6,000 distinct thoughts per day, a figure the researchers described as 'thought worms' — discrete bursts of neural activity that mark the transition from one idea to the next.

components.note: 甩 is visually the character 用 ('to use') with an added stroke pulled outward from the frame — as if something is being flung out of use, giving 甩 its meaning 'to throw, to fling, to discard.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 她终于甩掉了那个不良习惯。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú shuǎidiào le nàge bùliáng xíguàn.
example.english: She finally got rid of that bad habit.
example.fact: MIT neuroscientist Ann Graybiel's research identified the basal ganglia as the brain region that encodes habits as automatic 'cue-routine-reward' loops, which is why habits can persist even after the original motivation disappears. Contrary to the popular claim that it takes 21 days to break a habit, a 2009 University College London study found the real average is closer to 66 days, with wide variation depending on the behavior and the person.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — many traditional medicines were made from plants and herbs
约 (yuē) gives a sound related to 药's reading yào, from an older, closer pronunciation link
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'

example.hanzi: 这家药店出售各种药品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yàodiàn chūshòu gèzhǒng yàopǐn.
example.english: This pharmacy sells all kinds of medicines.
example.fact: Aspirin's active compound has roots in willow bark, which ancient Egyptian and Greek physicians used to relieve pain and fever thousands of years ago. Chemist Felix Hoffmann at the German company Bayer first synthesized a stable, less irritating version — acetylsalicylic acid — in 1897, and it remains one of the most widely used drugs in the world, with over 40,000 tons produced annually.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 暗 describes the absence of light, the opposite of a bright sun.
音 (yīn) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading àn has diverged.
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'

example.hanzi: 那位国王在1914年遭到暗杀。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi guówáng zài 1914 nián zāodào ànshā.
example.english: That king was assassinated in 1914.
example.fact: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary was assassinated in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, by Gavrilo Princip, a 19-year-old Bosnian Serb nationalist. The assassination set off a diplomatic crisis that escalated within weeks into World War I, ultimately drawing in over 30 countries and killing more than 16 million people.

components.note: 力 (strength) — relates to 办's meaning 'to handle, manage, do,' something accomplished through effort.
八 (bā) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from bàn.
事 pictures a hand at the bottom holding a forked instrument or record-tool used by an official above, the source of its meaning 'affair, matter, to serve, to work.'

example.hanzi: 他去政府部门办事，排了很长时间的队。
example.pinyin: Tā qù zhèngfǔ bùmén bànshì, pái le hěn cháng shíjiān de duì.
example.english: He went to a government department to handle some business and waited in a long line.
example.fact: In 1955, British historian C. Northcote Parkinson observed what became known as 'Parkinson's Law of bureaucracy': that administrative staff in an organization tend to multiply at a fixed rate of about 5-7 percent per year regardless of the actual amount of work to be done. Estonia has taken the opposite approach since the 2000s, digitizing nearly all government services so that citizens can file taxes, vote, and register a business online in minutes rather than visiting an office in person.

components.note: 异 (a simplified form of 異) depicts a person with upraised hands and an odd expression, suggesting something strange or different.
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 青春期的孩子开始对异性产生好感。
example.pinyin: Qīngchūnqī de háizi kāishǐ duì yìxìng chǎnshēng hǎogǎn.
example.english: Children in puberty begin to develop feelings for the opposite sex.
example.fact: Puberty begins when the hypothalamus starts releasing gonadotropin-releasing hormone in pulses, which in turn signals the pituitary gland to release hormones that trigger the ovaries or testes to mature. The average onset age has been dropping globally for over a century — in the mid-1800s the average girl had her first period around age 17, while today the global average is closer to 12, a shift researchers link partly to improved nutrition.

components.note: 儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.
艹 (grass) forms the top of the character.
木 (tree), sheltered beneath a covering, together depict plants flourishing, giving 荣 its meaning 'glory, prosperity.'

example.hanzi: 为国家赢得奥运金牌是一件光荣的事。
example.pinyin: Wèi guójiā yíngdé Àoyùn jīnpái shì yí jiàn guāngróng de shì.
example.english: Winning an Olympic gold medal for one's country is a glorious thing.
example.fact: The ancient Olympic Games, first recorded in 776 BC at Olympia in Greece, didn't award gold medals at all — winners received a simple wreath cut from a sacred olive tree, along with enormous social prestige back home. The modern gold-silver-bronze medal system wasn't introduced until the 1904 St. Louis Games; earlier revivals of the modern Olympics in 1896 and 1900 gave silver medals to first place and bronze to second.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
The 田-shaped top pictures a large, strange head.
儿-shaped legs below trace a crouching, spindly body, together giving 鬼 the shape of a ghostly figure.

example.hanzi: 妈妈笑着说这个小鬼又调皮了。
example.pinyin: Māma xiào zhe shuō zhège xiǎoguǐ yòu tiáopí le.
example.english: Mom laughed and said this little imp was being mischievous again.
example.fact: The idea of mischievous small demons or imps appears across cultures independently, from European goblins to Japanese oni and West African trickster spirits, and folklorists suggest this may reflect a near-universal way of explaining unexplained mishaps — a spilled bucket of milk or a lost object — before germ theory or simple forgetfulness became the default explanation. Ireland's Halloween tradition of carving turnips, later pumpkins in America, to ward off wandering spirits is one direct descendant of these old imp-warding customs.

components.note: 贝 (money) — bestowing a gift is tied to giving something of value.
易 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to cì, having drifted apart over time.
予 pictures a weaving shuttle passed from one hand to another, the source of its meaning 'to give, to grant.'

example.hanzi: 古代皇帝常常赐予功臣土地和财富。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài huángdì chángcháng cìyǔ gōngchén tǔdì hé cáifù.
example.english: Ancient emperors often granted land and wealth to meritorious officials.
example.fact: In ancient Rome, the patron-client relationship structured much of public life: wealthy patrons granted money, legal protection, or land to clients in exchange for political support and public displays of loyalty each morning at the patron's house, a ritual called the salutatio. Similar exchange systems, such as feudal land grants in medieval Europe or the fief system in Japan, recur throughout history as ways rulers secured loyalty before large bureaucracies or currency economies existed.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows 逻 relates to movement, as in patrolling on foot.
罗 (luó) gives the exact sound of 逻.
车 (cart) — 辑 originally referred to fitting a cart's parts together, extending to 'gather, compile, edit.'
咠 (qì) is distantly related in sound to jí, sharing the same historical initial series (j/q/x) though the two have drifted apart.

example.hanzi: 他的推理完全符合逻辑。
example.pinyin: Tā de tuīlǐ wánquán fúhé luóji.
example.english: His reasoning is completely logical.
example.fact: George Boole, a self-taught English mathematician, published 'An Investigation of the Laws of Thought' in 1854, introducing what became known as Boolean algebra — a system reducing logical reasoning to combinations of true and false. Nearly a century later, Claude Shannon realized Boole's algebra could be implemented with electrical switches, laying the theoretical foundation for every digital computer built since.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 违 involves stepping away from what is required, i.e. disobeying.
韦 (wéi) is an exact match for the sound of 违.
⺼ (flesh/body) — 背 refers to the back, a part of the body
北 (běi) gives a sound close to 背's reading bèi, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他的行为违背了公司的规章制度。
example.pinyin: Tā de xíngwéi wéibèi le gōngsī de guīzhāng zhìdù.
example.english: His behavior violated the company's rules and regulations.
example.fact: In June 1941, Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa against the Soviet Union, violating the Molotov-Ribbentrop non-aggression pact the two countries had signed less than two years earlier in 1939. The surprise invasion, involving over 3 million troops along a front stretching nearly 2,900 kilometers, remains the largest land invasion in military history.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 瞬 describes the blink of an eye, an instant.
舜 (shùn) gives the sound — an exact match with 瞬.
门 (door/gate) — 间 pictures light passing through an entryway.
日 (sun) — sunlight shining through a gap in a doorway gave 间 its meaning of a space 'in between,' as in 中间 (in the middle) or 时间 (time, the space between moments).

example.hanzi: 那一瞬间，他终于明白了真相。
example.pinyin: Nà yí shùnjiān, tā zhōngyú míngbái le zhēnxiàng.
example.english: In that instant, he finally understood the truth.
example.fact: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for experiments that generate attosecond pulses of light — each lasting roughly one billionth of a billionth of a second — brief enough to capture the motion of electrons inside atoms, which had previously been too fast to observe directly. To put that in perspective, an attosecond is to one second what one second is to about 31.7 billion years.

components.note: 酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar
The 田-shaped top pictures a large, strange head.
儿-shaped legs below trace a crouching, spindly body, together giving 鬼 the shape of a ghostly figure.

example.hanzi: 邻居都知道他是个酒鬼。
example.pinyin: Línjū dōu zhīdào tā shì ge jiǔguǐ.
example.english: The neighbors all know he is a drunkard.
example.fact: About a third of people of East Asian descent carry a genetic variant of the ALDH2 enzyme that makes it harder to break down acetaldehyde, a toxic byproduct of alcohol metabolism. This causes the well-known 'Asian flush' — rapid facial reddening, nausea, and a faster heartbeat after drinking — and carriers of this variant who drink heavily anyway face a significantly elevated risk of esophageal cancer.

components.note: 一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.

example.hanzi: 上课的时候要正经一点，别开玩笑。
example.pinyin: Shàngkè de shíhou yào zhèngjīng yìdiǎn, bié kāi wánxiào.
example.english: Be a bit more proper during class, don't joke around.
example.fact: Victorian England produced an enormous market for etiquette manuals, with titles like 'Manners and Rules of Good Society' selling widely from the 1830s onward and dictating everything from how long to leave a calling card to the precise angle of a bow. Modern etiquette researchers note that such formalized codes of propriety often emerge most strongly in societies undergoing rapid social mobility, functioning as a way for the newly wealthy middle class to signal status alongside the old aristocracy.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — suggests departing or leaving.
贵 (valuable, precious) — leaving something valuable behind gave 遗 its meaning 'to lose, to leave behind.'
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.hanzi: 长城是中国重要的文化遗产。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng shì Zhōngguó zhòngyào de wénhuà yíchǎn.
example.english: The Great Wall is an important cultural heritage of China.
example.fact: UNESCO's World Heritage program was established in 1972 to protect sites of outstanding cultural or natural value, and it now lists more than 1,200 sites across over 160 countries. The Great Wall of China, inscribed in 1987, is not actually a single continuous wall but a network of walls, fortifications, and watchtowers built and rebuilt by different dynasties over roughly 2,000 years, with a total length — including all branches — estimated at more than 21,000 kilometers.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.
彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这条小路通往山顶的寺庙。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiǎolù tōngwǎng shāndǐng de sìmiào.
example.english: This small path leads to the temple on the mountaintop.
example.fact: The Inca road network, built without the wheel or draft animals, stretched an estimated 40,000 kilometers across the Andes, connecting the empire from present-day Ecuador to Chile. Relay runners called chasquis carried messages along it in a system fast enough to relay news roughly 400 kilometers a day, comparable to modern postal speeds of the era, achieved entirely on foot through some of the world's most mountainous terrain.

components.note: 牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他在大学里主修物理专业。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ zhǔxiū wùlǐ zhuānyè.
example.english: He majored in physics in university.
example.fact: On July 4, 2012, physicists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider announced the discovery of the Higgs boson, the particle responsible for giving other particles mass, confirming a mechanism first proposed by Peter Higgs and others in 1964. Finding it required smashing protons together at nearly the speed of light inside a 27-kilometer circular tunnel and sifting through roughly a quadrillion collisions to spot the extraordinarily rare signature of the particle's decay.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — 圈 describes an enclosed loop or pen, as in 'circle, corral.'
卷 (juǎn) shares the rhyme -uan with quān, though the initial has drifted from j- to q- over time.
大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'

example.hanzi: 他意识到自己掉进了一个圈套。
example.pinyin: Tā yìshi dào zìjǐ diào jìn le yí ge quāntào.
example.english: He realized he had fallen into a trap.
example.fact: The Venus flytrap snaps shut in about one-tenth of a second, one of the fastest movements in the plant kingdom, triggered only when tiny trigger hairs inside the trap are touched twice within roughly 20 seconds — a safeguard that keeps the plant from wasting energy snapping shut on raindrops or debris. Charles Darwin studied the plant extensively and called it 'one of the most wonderful in the world.'

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) shows 肥 relates to a bodily state.
巴 (bā) gives a sound distantly related to féi, having drifted apart over time.

皂 originally referred to the soapberry, a fruit whose pulp was used to make an early soap-like cleanser; the character later extended to mean 'black' from the fruit's dark color, and by extension 'soap' in modern usage.

example.hanzi: 洗手的时候要用肥皂彻底清洁双手。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒu de shíhou yào yòng féizào chèdǐ qīngjié shuāngshǒu.
example.english: When washing your hands, you should use soap to thoroughly clean them.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found evidence of soap-like substances on Babylonian clay tablets dating to around 2800 BC, made by boiling fats with wood ash. Soap works because its molecules have a water-loving head and a fat-loving tail, letting them surround grease particles and lift them off skin into water that would otherwise never mix with oil — the same chemistry, called an amphiphilic structure, that makes modern detergents effective today.
